correctness.rationale: Squarefreeness follows from f’=x⁴(x⁵−a): the only repeated-root condition is a²=1. In basis x^{j-1}dx/y, coefficient extraction [x^{3i−j}]f yields H with nonzero entries 1,a,a,1 at (1,3),(2,1),(3,4),(4,2), det=-a². For a≠0 H invertible and the Jacobian ordinary. At a=0 its rank is2 and H H^(3)=0, so p-rank0 and a-number2. Two explicit tame involutions have genus2 quotients; their Jacobians split up to degree16 prime-to-3 isogeny, and each genus2 factor with p-rank0 has only slopes1/2, so the original has eight 1/2 slopes. Independently reconstructed H and determinant and verified its square at zero. Marked-coordinate divisor multiplicity 2, quotient u=a² multiplicity 1; no full coarse-moduli assertion.

value.rationale: The full marked one-parameter Newton-polygon stratification for a natural dihedral genus-four family is an exact useful degeneration boundary. Identifying the doubled Hasse determinant, the quotient-normalized simple equation, and a supersingular but not superspecial special fiber provides more than a single existence example, although the fixed-family calculation is narrow. The result is useful in identifying which members of the known special family are ordinary; it is not credited with the quotient isogeny itself.

final_claim: For the smooth char3 reciprocal hyperelliptic genus-four family y²=x^10+a x^5+1 (a²≠1), every a≠0 is ordinary, while a=0 is supersingular with a-number2; the Hasse determinant -a² has one doubled zero on the marked line and one simple zero under u=a².
